resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §45 (Per-exercise leap test: 3 observable Monday outcomes) line 103: scope: The judge's counts are correct. Lines 103-145 hold the maintainer block and contain Plug points, Watch-fors, Why 35 minutes and View summary. `grep -i leap` and `grep -i monday` on the file return nothing. The cited rule is also read correctly: §45 in `check_pedagogy.md` says "Every exercise maintainer block: 3 observable outcomes student exhibits on own codebase by next working day." The finding still fails on scope, lens (d), because it binds an engineer-framed rule to an exercise whose audience has no codebase.

1. **Wording and audience.**
   - §45 is written for engineers: "own codebase", "worktree", "CLAUDE.local.md". Its origin is the legacy AE101 megaeval axes, per the compounded entry 2026-05-03.
   - This exercise is Agents 101 Module 4. Its students are CTOs, SVPs and other builder-leaders. §35 and the self-study skill describe them as "not a developer". The exercise's own "What you do" has them audit "the system you built in modules 2-3", not a codebase.
   - The judge says the M5/M6 arc-mood carve-out does not apply, and that is true. But its fix example ("owns a reusable audit skill...") is carve-out-style wording. That wording is only licensed for M5/M6.

2. **Training convention.**
   - Of the 18 exercises linked from the Agents 101 module files, 14 contain no "leap". Those 14 include author-security-skill, extend-your-system, eval-loop, name-your-challenge, personal-agent-homework and build-for-the-gap. Only the three sharing-plan/share-your-work exercises and personal-site-with-guardrails carry one.
   - Earlier judge instances ruled §45 N/A for Agents 101 exercises. `author-security-skill.pedagogy` said "leap tests are an AE101/APT101 convention; 0 of 4 sampled A101 exercises carry one, training-level call". `build-for-the-gap.pedagogy` said "A101 exercises carry none by training convention; rule's 'own codebase' frame is engineer-side". `build-your-challenge-memory.story` and `build-for-the-gap.story` also returned N/A, and `extend-your-system.pedagogy` returned PASS.
   - Other judges returned REVISE on the same absence in `eval-loop`, `hallucination-bakeoff` and `build-your-challenge-memory`. Only this finding and the `joint-double-diamond` REVISE are blocking. The file-by-file REVISE verdicts are inconsistent, and the pairing of this file's blocking verdict with its prior PASS shows noise.
   - This file's own Quality stamp reads "pedagogy PASS" (2026-08-25, pedagogy@725101ec) with the same absence of a leap test. That is a prior pass on the identical surface.

3. **Other lenses.**
   - I found no dated accept-note that pre-authorises the absence. The stamp is the only trace.
   - Line 103 is inside the maintainer block, so the placement lens (e) does not help the refutation.
   - The rule says the story judge blocks ship on a missing leap test. It does not name the pedagogy judge as the blocker.

Conclusion: the open question is whether §45 should apply to Agents 101 at all. That is a training-level rule question for the maintainer, not a per-file BLOCK. The exercise should not be treated as defective on §45.
